mishnayos.summary: There are four "New Years" in the Jewish year, and each one is used for counting something different: kings and Yamim Tovim, maaser of animals, years, and trees.

chunks.en: There are four New Years.
chunks.st: They are four days in the year that serve as the New Year, each for a different purpose:

chunks.he: בְּאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לַמְּלָכִים וְלָרְגָלִים.
chunks.en: On the first of Nisan is the New Year for kings and for the Yamim Tovim.
chunks.st: On the first of Nisan is the New Year for kings; it is from this date that the years of a king’s rule are counted. And the first of Nisan is also the New Year for the order of the Festivals,
chunks.stMore: as it determines which is considered the first Festival of the year and which the last.

words.note: The years of a king's rule are counted from Nisan.
Nisan decides which Yom Tov is first in the year.

chunks.he: בְּאֶחָד בֶּאֱלוּל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה.
chunks.en: On the first of Elul is the New Year for maaser of animals.
chunks.explain: Animals born before this day are counted with last year's animals.
chunks.st: On the first of Elul is the New Year for animal tithes;
chunks.stMore: all the animals born prior to that date belong to the previous tithe year and are tithed as a single unit, whereas those born after that date belong to the next tithe year.

words.note: A tenth part, set aside for Hashem.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:

chunks.en: it is on the first of Tishrei.
chunks.st: The New Year for animal tithes is on the first of Tishrei.

chunks.en: On the first of Tishrei is the New Year
chunks.st: On the first of Tishrei is the New Year for

chunks.en: for counting years, for Shemittah years, and for Yovel years,
chunks.st: counting years, as will be explained in the Gemara; for calculating Sabbatical Years and Jubilee Years,
chunks.stMore: i.e., from the first of Tishrei there is a biblical prohibition to work the land during these years;

words.note: Every seventh year, when we do not work the land.
The fiftieth year.

chunks.en: for planting, and for vegetables.
chunks.st: for planting, for determining the years of orla, the three-year period from when a tree has been planted during which time its fruit is forbidden; and for tithing vegetables,
chunks.stMore: as vegetables picked prior to that date cannot be tithed together with vegetables picked after that date.

words.note: To count the first three years of a new tree, when its fruit is forbidden (orlah).
For taking maaser from vegetables.

chunks.en: On the first of Shevat
chunks.st: On the first of Shevat

chunks.en: is the New Year for trees.
chunks.st: is the New Year for the tree;
chunks.stMore: the fruit of a tree that was formed prior to that date belong to the previous tithe year and cannot be tithed together with fruit that was formed after that date;

words.note: For taking maaser from the fruit of trees.

chunks.en: That is what Beis Shammai say.
chunks.st: this ruling is in accordance with the statement of Beit Shammai.

chunks.en: But Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: But Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: it is on the fifteenth of Shevat.
chunks.st: The New Year for trees is on the fifteenth of Shevat.

words.note: Tu BiShvat.

mishnayos.summary: Hashem judges the world at four times of the year. On Rosh Hashanah, every person in the world passes before Him to be judged.

chunks.en: The world is judged at four times of the year.
chunks.st: At four times of the year the world is judged:

chunks.en: On Pesach, about grain.
chunks.st: On Passover judgment is passed concerning grain;

chunks.en: On Shavuos, about fruit of the trees.
chunks.st: on Shavuot concerning fruits that grow on a tree;

words.note: Atzeres is another name for Shavuos.

chunks.en: On Rosh Hashanah, all the people of the world
chunks.st: on Rosh HaShana, all creatures

chunks.en: pass before Hashem like sheep, one by one,
chunks.st: pass before Him like sheep [benei maron],
chunks.basisNote: "One by one" is how Bartenura explains it.

words.note: Sheep that walk one at a time through a narrow gate to be counted.

chunks.en: as it says in Tehillim: "He forms all their hearts together,
chunks.st: as it is stated: “He Who fashions their hearts alike,

chunks.en: He understands all that they do."
chunks.st: Who considers all their deeds” (Psalms 33:15);

chunks.en: And on Sukkos they are judged about water.
chunks.st: and on the festival of Sukkot they are judged concerning water, i.e., the rainfall of the coming year.

words.note: Sukkos.
The rain of the coming year.

mishnayos.summary: The Beis Din in Yerushalayim decided which day was Rosh Chodesh. In six months they sent messengers far away to tell people, so they would keep the Yamim Tovim on the right day.

chunks.en: The messengers go out for six months:
chunks.explain: To tell everyone which day was Rosh Chodesh.
chunks.st: In six months of the year the messengers go out
chunks.stMore: from the court in Jerusalem to report throughout Eretz Yisrael and the Diaspora which day was established as the New Moon, the thirtieth or the thirty-first day since the previous New Moon.

chunks.en: for Nisan, because of Pesach;
chunks.st: They go out in the month of Nisan, due to Passover,
chunks.stMore: so that people will know on which day to celebrate it;

chunks.en: for Av, because of the fast;
chunks.st: in the month of Av, due to the fast of the Ninth of Av;

words.note: Tisha B'Av.

chunks.en: for Elul, because of Rosh Hashanah;
chunks.st: in Elul, due to Rosh HaShana,
chunks.stMore: which begins thirty days after the New Moon of Elul;

chunks.en: for Tishrei, to set the right days for the Yamim Tovim;
chunks.st: in Tishrei, due to the need to establish the correct dates on which to celebrate the Festivals of Tishrei, i.e., Yom Kippur and Sukkot;

words.note: Yom Kippur and Sukkos.

chunks.en: for Kislev, because of Chanukah;
chunks.st: in Kislev, due to Hanukkah;

chunks.en: and for Adar, because of Purim.
chunks.st: and in Adar, due to Purim.

chunks.en: And when the Beis HaMikdash was standing,
chunks.st: And when the Temple was standing,

chunks.en: they also went out for Iyar,
chunks.st: messengers would also go out in the month of Iyyar

chunks.en: because of Pesach Sheni, the "small Pesach."
chunks.st: due to small Passover,
chunks.stMore: i.e., second Pesaḥ, which occurs on the fourteenth of Iyyar. This holiday allowed those who were ritually impure or on a distant journey on the fourteenth of Nisan, and therefore incapable of bringing the Paschal lamb at that time, to bring their Paschal lamb a month later.

words.note: Pesach Sheni, on the fourteenth of Iyar.

mishnayos.summary: Witnesses who saw the new moon may break Shabbos to come tell the Beis Din, but only for Nisan and Tishrei. When the Beis HaMikdash stood, they did so for every month.

chunks.he: עַל שְׁנֵי חֳדָשִׁים מְחַלְּלִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
chunks.en: For two months, witnesses may break Shabbos:
chunks.explain: To travel and tell Beis Din they saw the new moon.
chunks.st: Only for the sake of two months may witnesses who saw the new moon desecrate Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: should that be necessary in order for them to offer testimony before the court:

words.note: Do work that is usually not allowed.

chunks.en: for Nisan and for Tishrei,
chunks.st: For the month of Nisan and for the month of Tishrei,

chunks.en: because in these months the messengers go out to Syria,
chunks.st: for in these months messengers are sent out to Syria,

chunks.en: and by them the Yamim Tovim are set.
chunks.st: and by them, i.e., these months, the dates of the major Festivals are set: Yom Kippur, Sukkot, Passover, and Shavuot.

chunks.en: And when the Beis HaMikdash was standing,
chunks.st: And when the Temple was standing,

chunks.en: they broke Shabbos for all the months,
chunks.st: the witnesses desecrated Shabbat for the fixing of the New Moon of all the months,

chunks.en: so the korban of Rosh Chodesh would be brought at the right time.
chunks.st: due to the imperative of fixing the proper offering of the New Moon at the correct time.

words.note: The special korban brought on Rosh Chodesh.

mishnayos.summary: May witnesses break Shabbos to report the new moon even if everyone could see it clearly? The Tanna Kamma says yes; Rabbi Yosei says no.

chunks.en: Whether the new moon was seen clearly
chunks.st: Whether the new moon was seen clearly [ba’alil] by everyone

chunks.en: or it was not seen clearly,
chunks.st: or whether it was not clearly seen,

chunks.en: witnesses may break Shabbos for it.
chunks.st: one may desecrate Shabbat in order to testify before the court.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: If it was seen clearly,
chunks.st: If the moon was clearly seen,

chunks.en: they may not break Shabbos for it.
chunks.explain: Other witnesses, closer to Yerushalayim, surely saw it too.
chunks.st: they may not desecrate Shabbat for it,
chunks.stMore: since other witnesses, located nearer to the court, will certainly testify. If these distant witnesses go to court to testify, they will desecrate Shabbat unnecessarily.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva once stopped many witnesses from breaking Shabbos to travel. Rabban Gamliel told him that this might make people stop coming when they are needed.

chunks.en: Once, more than forty pairs of witnesses were passing by,
chunks.st: There was once an incident where more than forty pairs of witnesses were passing
chunks.stMore: through on their way to Jerusalem to testify about the new moon,

words.note: Something that really happened.

chunks.en: and Rabbi Akiva held them back in Lod.
chunks.explain: He told them they did not need to break Shabbos.
chunks.st: and Rabbi Akiva detained them in Lod,
chunks.stMore: telling them that there was no need for them to desecrate Shabbat for this purpose.

words.note: A city in Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel sent a message to him:
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel sent a message to him:

chunks.en: "If you hold back the many people,
chunks.st: If you detain the many
chunks.stMore: people who wish to testify about the new moon,

chunks.en: you will make them stumble in the future."
chunks.explain: Next time they may not come, even when they are needed.
chunks.st: you will cause them to stumble in the future.
chunks.stMore: They will say: Why should we go, seeing that our testimony is unnecessary? At some point they will be needed, and no witnesses will come to the court.

mishnayos.summary: Can a father and son be witnesses together for the new moon? This mishnah brings two opinions, and a story about Toviyah the doctor.

chunks.en: If a father and his son saw the new moon,
chunks.st: If a father and his son saw the new moon,

chunks.he: יֵלְכוּ. לֹא שֶׁמִּצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה,
chunks.en: they should both go. Not that they can join together as witnesses,
chunks.explain: Close relatives cannot be witnesses together.
chunks.st: they should both go to the court in Jerusalem. It is not that they can join together
chunks.stMore: to give testimony, for close relatives are disqualified from testifying together,

chunks.en: but so that if one of them may not be a witness,
chunks.st: but they both go so that if one of them is disqualified,

words.note: Not allowed to be a witness.

chunks.en: the other one can join with someone else.
chunks.st: the second may join together with another witness to testify about the new moon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: a father and his son and all relatives
chunks.st: A father and his son and all their relatives

chunks.en: may be witnesses for the new moon.
chunks.st: are fit to combine together as witnesses for testimony to determine the start of the month.

words.note: Allowed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.en: There was a story with Toviyah the doctor,
chunks.st: There was an incident with Toviyya the doctor.

chunks.en: who saw the new moon in Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: When he saw the new moon in Jerusalem,

chunks.en: he, his son, and his servant who had been set free.
chunks.st: he and his son and his freed slave all went to testify.

chunks.en: The Kohanim accepted him and his son,
chunks.st: The priests accepted him and his son as witnesses

chunks.en: but did not accept his servant.
chunks.explain: They wanted only witnesses who were born Jewish.
chunks.st: and disqualified his slave,
chunks.stMore: for they ruled stringently that the month may be sanctified only on the basis of the testimony of those of Jewish lineage.

chunks.en: And when they came before the Beis Din,
chunks.st: And when they came before the court,

chunks.en: they accepted him and his servant,
chunks.st: they accepted him and his slave as witnesses

chunks.en: but did not accept his son.
chunks.explain: Because a father and son are relatives.
chunks.st: and disqualified his son, due to the familial relationship.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists people who may not be witnesses, like people who gamble or charge interest, because they cannot be trusted.

chunks.en: These are the people who may not be witnesses:
chunks.st: The following are unfit
chunks.stMore: to give testimony, as they are considered thieves and robbers:

chunks.en: one who plays dice for money,
chunks.st: One who plays with dice [kubbiyya] or other games of chance for money;

words.note: A game of luck played for money.

chunks.en: people who lend money for interest,
chunks.st: and those who lend money with interest;

words.note: Extra money charged for a loan.

chunks.en: people who race pigeons,
chunks.st: and those who race pigeons and place wagers on the outcome;

words.note: They bet money on which pigeon will win.

chunks.en: people who trade in Shemittah fruit,
chunks.st: and merchants who deal in produce of the Sabbatical Year,
chunks.stMore: which may be eaten, but may not be an object of commerce;

words.note: Fruit of Shemittah may be eaten, but not used for business.

chunks.en: and servants. This is the rule:
chunks.st: and slaves. This is the principle:

chunks.he: כָּל עֵדוּת שֶׁאֵין הָאִשָּׁה כְשֵׁרָה לָהּ,
chunks.en: any testimony for which a woman is not allowed,
chunks.st: Any testimony for which a woman is unfit,

chunks.en: these people are also not allowed.
chunks.st: these too are unfit.
chunks.stMore: Although in certain cases a woman’s testimony is accepted, e.g., to testify to the death of someone’s husband, in the majority of cases her testimony is not valid.

mishnayos.summary: Witnesses of the new moon must get to Yerushalayim, even on Shabbos. They may ride, carry sticks for safety, and bring food, because the Yamim Tovim must be on time.

chunks.en: Someone who saw the new moon
chunks.st: With regard to one who saw the new moon

chunks.en: but cannot walk,
chunks.st: but is unable to go
chunks.stMore: to Jerusalem by foot because he is sick or has difficulty walking,

chunks.en: they may bring him on a donkey,
chunks.st: others may bring him on a donkey or

chunks.en: or even in a bed.
chunks.st: even in a bed, even on Shabbat if necessary.

chunks.en: And if robbers are hiding to catch them,
chunks.st: And if the witnesses are concerned that bandits may be lying in wait for them along the road,

words.note: Someone hiding to attack.

chunks.en: they may take sticks in their hands.
chunks.st: they may take clubs or other weapons in their hands, even on Shabbat.

chunks.en: And if the way was far,
chunks.st: And if it was a long journey to Jerusalem,

chunks.en: they may take food with them.
chunks.st: they may take sustenance with them,
chunks.stMore: although it is ordinarily prohibited to carry on Shabbat,

chunks.en: Because for a trip of a night and a day, they may break
chunks.st: since for a distance of a walk of a night and a day, the witnesses may desecrate

chunks.en: Shabbos and go out to tell about the new moon,
chunks.st: Shabbat and go out to give testimony to determine the start of the month.

chunks.en: as it says in Vayikra,
chunks.st: This is as it is stated:

chunks.en: "These are the Yamim Tovim of Hashem, which
chunks.st: “These are the Festivals of the Lord, sacred gatherings,

chunks.en: you shall call at their right time."
chunks.st: which you shall declare in their seasons”
chunks.stMore: (Leviticus 23:4). This teaches that, in all cases, the Festivals must be fixed at their proper times, even if it entails the transgression of Torah prohibitions.

mishnayos.summary: A witness for the new moon must be someone the Beis Din knows. After some people sent false witnesses, the Sages made a rule to accept only witnesses they know.

chunks.en: If the Beis Din does not know him,
chunks.st: If the members of the Great Sanhedrin in Jerusalem are not familiar with that
chunks.stMore: one who saw the new moon, i.e., that he is a valid witness, the members of his local court of twenty-three

chunks.en: his town sends another person with him to say he is a good witness.
chunks.st: send another with him to testify about him.

chunks.en: At first, they would accept witnesses
chunks.st: The mishna adds: Initially, the court would accept testimony to determine the start

chunks.en: about the new moon from any person.
chunks.st: of the month from any person,
chunks.stMore: as all are presumed to be qualified witnesses, absent any disqualifying factors.

chunks.en: When the minim spoiled it,
chunks.explain: They sent false witnesses on purpose.
chunks.st: However, when the Boethusians, a sect whose members had their own opinions with regard to the establishment of the Festivals, corrupted
chunks.stMore: the process by sending false witnesses to testify about the new moon,

words.note: The Baisusim, a group who did not follow the Sages.

chunks.en: the Sages made a rule that they would accept witnesses
chunks.st: the Sages instituted that they would accept this testimony

chunks.en: only from people they know.
chunks.st: only from those men familiar to the Sanhedrin as valid witnesses.

mishnayos.summary: At first, the news of Rosh Chodesh was spread by lighting fires on mountaintops. When the Kusim tricked people with false fires, messengers were sent instead.

chunks.en: At first, they would light torches.
chunks.explain: On mountaintops, to show far away that it was Rosh Chodesh.
chunks.st: Initially, after the court sanctified the new month they would light torches
chunks.stMore: on the mountaintops, from one peak to another, to signal to the community in Babylonia that the month had been sanctified.

chunks.en: When the Kusim spoiled it,
chunks.explain: They lit torches at the wrong times to confuse people.
chunks.st: After the Samaritans [Kutim] corrupted
chunks.stMore: and ruined this method by lighting torches at the wrong times to confuse the Jews,

words.note: Samaritans, a people who lived in Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: the Sages made a rule that messengers should go out.
chunks.st: the Sages instituted that messengers should go out
chunks.stMore: to the Diaspora and inform them of the start of the month.

mishnayos.summary: How did they send the message with torches? They lit a torch on a mountain and waved it until they saw the next mountain wave a torch too.

chunks.en: How would they light the torches?
chunks.st: The mishna asks: How would they light the torches during that earlier period?

chunks.en: They brought long poles of cedar wood,
chunks.st: They would bring items that burn well, e.g., long poles of cedar,

chunks.en: and reeds, and pine wood, and threads of
chunks.st: reeds, pinewood, and beaten

words.note: Wood that burns well.

chunks.en: flax, and he tied them with a string.
chunks.st: flax, and tie them together with a string.

chunks.en: And he went up to the top of the mountain and lit
chunks.st: And someone would then ascend to the top of the mountain and light

chunks.en: a fire with them.
chunks.st: the torch on fire with them,

chunks.en: And he waved it back and forth, and up and down,
chunks.st: and wave it back and forth and up and down,

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁהוּא רוֹאֶה אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ שֶׁהוּא
chunks.en: until he saw his friend
chunks.st: until he would see his colleague

chunks.en: doing the same on top of the second mountain.
chunks.st: doing likewise on the top of the second mountain.
chunks.stMore: In this manner he would know that the next messenger had received the message and passed it on.

chunks.en: And so on the top of the third mountain.
chunks.st: And similarly, the second torchbearer would wait for a signal from the one on the top of the third mountain,
chunks.stMore: and so on. In this manner the message would reach the Diaspora.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah names the mountains where the torches were lit, from Yerushalayim all the way until the whole golah was lit up like one big fire.

chunks.en: And from where did they light the torches?
chunks.st: And from which mountains would they light the torches?

chunks.en: From Har HaMishchah to Sartava,
chunks.st: They would transmit the message from the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem to Sartava,

words.note: Har HaZeisim, the Mount of Olives, by Yerushalayim.
A mountain.

chunks.en: and from Sartava to Grofina,
chunks.st: and from Sartava to Gerofina,

chunks.en: and from Grofina to Chavran,
chunks.st: and from Gerofina to Ḥavran,

chunks.en: and from Chavran to Beis Biltin.
chunks.st: and from Ḥavran to Beit Baltin.

chunks.en: And from Beis Biltin they did not move on to another place.
chunks.st: And from Beit Baltin they would not move
chunks.stMore: to light torches in any other predetermined location.

chunks.en: Instead, he waved the torch back and forth, and up and down,
chunks.st: Rather, the one who was appointed for this task would wave the torch back and forth and up and down,

chunks.en: until he saw the whole golah
chunks.st: until he would see the entire Diaspora

words.note: The Jews living outside Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: lit up before him like one big bonfire.
chunks.st: before him alight like one large bonfire,
chunks.stMore: as they would light torches to continue transmitting the message from place to place all the way to the farthest reaches of the Diaspora.

mishnayos.summary: Witnesses for the new moon gathered in a big courtyard in Yerushalayim and were treated well. Rabban Gamliel the Elder let them walk two thousand amos on Shabbos, and also others who come to help.

chunks.en: There was a big courtyard in Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: There was a large courtyard in Jerusalem,

chunks.en: and it was called Beis Yaazek.
chunks.st: which was called Beit Ya’zek.

chunks.en: All the witnesses gathered there,
chunks.st: And there all the witnesses coming to testify about the new moon would gather,

chunks.en: and the Beis Din checked them there.
chunks.st: and the court of seventy-one judges would examine them there.

chunks.en: And they made big meals for them,
chunks.st: And they would prepare great feasts for them,

chunks.en: so that they would be happy to come again.
chunks.st: so that they would be willing and accustomed to coming and submitting their testimony.

chunks.en: At first, they would not move
chunks.st: Initially, when witnesses would arrive on Shabbat from a distant place, they would not move

chunks.en: from there the whole day.
chunks.explain: On Shabbos, they had walked past the Shabbos limit to get there.
chunks.st: from there all day,
chunks.stMore: as they had left their Shabbat limit, and it was consequently prohibited for them to walk more than four cubits in any direction once they had completed their mission. Concerned that this limitation would discourage witnesses from coming,

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel the Elder made a rule that they may
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel the Elder instituted that the witnesses be permitted to

chunks.en: walk two thousand amos in every direction.
chunks.st: walk two thousand cubits in each direction. The mishna continues:

words.note: An amah is about the length of an arm.

chunks.en: And not only these people,
chunks.st: And not only these
chunks.stMore: witnesses are granted two thousand cubits from their new place,

chunks.en: but also a midwife who comes to help a baby be born,
chunks.st: but this applies also to a midwife who comes to deliver a child,

words.note: A woman who helps when a baby is born.

chunks.en: and someone who comes to save people from a fire, or from
chunks.st: and one who comes to rescue Jews from a fire, from

chunks.en: an army, or from a river, or from a falling building.
chunks.st: an invasion of gentile troops, from a flooding river, or from the collapse of a building.

chunks.en: These are like the people of the city,
chunks.st: All these are considered like the inhabitants of the city where they arrive,

chunks.he: וְיֵשׁ לָהֶם אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכָל רוּחַ:
chunks.en: and they may walk two thousand amos in every direction.
chunks.st: and therefore they have two thousand cubits in each direction.

mishnayos.summary: The Beis Din checked the witnesses one at a time, asking exactly how and where they saw the moon. If both witnesses' answers matched, their testimony was accepted.

chunks.en: How do they check the witnesses?
chunks.st: How do they examine the witnesses who come to testify about the new moon?

chunks.en: The pair that came first,
chunks.st: They deal with them in order, as the pair of witnesses that arrives first

chunks.en: they check first.
chunks.st: they examine first.

chunks.he: וּמַכְנִיסִין אֶת הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבָּהֶן וְאוֹמְרִים לוֹ,
chunks.en: They bring in the older one and say to him,
chunks.st: They bring in the greater of the two witnesses, and they say to him:

chunks.st: or did the serpent preserve life?

chunks.he: אֶלָּא, בִּזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל מִסְתַּכְּלִין כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה
chunks.en: Rather, when Yisrael looked up
chunks.st: Rather, when the Jewish people turned their eyes upward

chunks.en: and gave their hearts to their Father in Heaven,
chunks.st: and subjected their hearts to their Father in Heaven,

chunks.en: they were healed.
chunks.st: they were healed,

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: but if not,

chunks.st: they rotted
chunks.stMore: from their snakebites. Returning to its halakhic discussion, the mishna continues:

chunks.en: A deaf person, a shoteh,
chunks.st: A deaf-mute, an imbecile,

words.note: Someone who cannot hear or speak.
Someone whose mind does not work properly.

chunks.he: וְקָטָן, אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן.
chunks.en: or a child cannot blow the shofar for everyone else.
chunks.st: or a minor who sounds the shofar cannot discharge the obligation on behalf of the community.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle with regard to similar matters:

chunks.en: Anyone who does not have to do a mitzvah
chunks.st: Whoever is not obligated to do a certain matter

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן:
chunks.en: cannot do it for everyone else.
chunks.st: cannot discharge the obligation on behalf of the community.

mishnayos.summary: When Rosh Hashanah fell on Shabbos, the shofar was blown only in the Beis HaMikdash. After it was destroyed, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made a rule to blow where there is a Beis Din.

chunks.en: When the Yom Tov of Rosh
chunks.st: With regard to the Festival day of Rosh HaShana

chunks.en: Hashanah falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: that occurs on Shabbat,

chunks.en: they would blow the shofar in the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: in the Temple they would sound the shofar as usual.

chunks.en: but not in the rest of the country.
chunks.st: However, they would not sound it in the rest of the country outside the Temple.

chunks.en: After the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
chunks.st: After the Temple was destroyed,

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made a rule
chunks.st: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted that

chunks.en: that they should blow in every place
chunks.st: the people should sound the shofar on Shabbat in every place

chunks.en: that has a Beis Din.
chunks.st: where there is a court of twenty-three judges.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar said:

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made the rule
chunks.st: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted this practice

chunks.en: only for Yavneh.
chunks.st: only in Yavne,
chunks.stMore: where the Great Sanhedrin of seventy-one judges resided in his time, but nowhere else.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: They said to him:

chunks.en: both Yavneh and every place
chunks.st: He instituted the practice both in Yavne and in any place

chunks.en: that has a Beis Din.
chunks.st: where there is a court.

mishnayos.summary: In the old days, towns near Yerushalayim also blew the shofar on Shabbos, but in Yavneh it was blown only in the Beis Din itself.

chunks.en: And Yerushalayim had one more thing
chunks.st: The mishna adds: And Jerusalem in earlier times had this additional

chunks.en: better than Yavneh:
chunks.st: superiority over Yavne
chunks.stMore: after Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted this practice,

chunks.en: any city that could see Yerushalayim
chunks.st: for in any city whose residents could see Jerusalem

chunks.en: and hear the shofar, and was close, and could come there,
chunks.st: and hear the sounding of the shofar from there, and which was near to Jerusalem and people could come to Jerusalem from there,

chunks.en: they would blow there. But in Yavneh they would blow
chunks.st: they would sound the shofar there as well, as it was considered part of Jerusalem. But in Yavne they would sound the shofar

chunks.en: only in the Beis Din.
chunks.st: only in the court itself, not in the surrounding cities.

mishnayos.summary: After the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made rules to remember it, like taking the lulav all seven days of Sukkos everywhere.

chunks.he: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיָה הַלּוּלָב נִטָּל בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ שִׁבְעָה,
chunks.en: At first, the lulav was taken in the Beis HaMikdash for seven days,
chunks.st: At first, during the Temple era, the lulav was taken in the Temple all seven days of Sukkot,

chunks.en: and in the rest of the country for one day.
chunks.st: and in the rest of the country outside the Temple, it was taken only one day, on the first day of the Festival.

chunks.en: After the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
chunks.st: After the Temple was destroyed,

chunks.he: הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי שֶׁיְהֵא
chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made a rule
chunks.st: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted that

chunks.he: לוּלָב נִטָּל בַּמְּדִינָה שִׁבְעָה זֵכֶר לַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
chunks.en: that the lulav be taken in the country for seven days, to remember the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: the lulav should be taken even in the rest of the country all seven days, in commemoration of the Temple.

chunks.en: and that on the whole day of waving the omer, new grain is forbidden.
chunks.explain: New grain may not be eaten all that day.
chunks.st: And for similar reasons, Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted that for the entire day of waving the omer offering, i.e., the sixteenth of Nisan, eating the grain of the new crop is prohibited.
chunks.stMore: By Torah law, when the Temple is standing the new grain may not be eaten until after the omer offering is brought on the sixteenth of Nisan, usually early in the morning. When the Temple is not standing it may be eaten from the time that the eastern horizon is illuminated at daybreak. However, Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted a prohibition against eating the new grain throughout the entire sixteenth of Nisan, until the seventeenth, to commemorate the Temple.

words.note: The day the omer was waved, the sixteenth of Nisan.

mishnayos.stIntro: After the previous mishna mentioned Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai’s ordinance that applies to the sounding of the shofar, this mishna records other ordinances instituted by the same Sage:

mishnayos.summary: At first, witnesses for the new moon were accepted all day, but after a mix-up with the Leviim's song, only until Minchah. Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai changed this back, and made another rule too.

chunks.en: At first, they would accept witnesses
chunks.st: Initially, they would accept testimony to determine the start

chunks.en: for the new moon all day long.
chunks.st: of the month throughout the entire thirtieth day
chunks.stMore: from the beginning of the month of Elul, before Rosh HaShana, and if witnesses arrived from afar and testified that they had sighted the New Moon the previous night, they would declare that day the Festival.

chunks.en: Once, the witnesses were late in coming,
chunks.st: Once, the witnesses tarried coming until the hour was late,

chunks.en: and the Leviim made a mistake in their song.
chunks.explain: They did not know if it was Yom Tov or a weekday.
chunks.st: and the Levites erred with regard to the song,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the psalm that they were supposed to recite, as they did not know at the time whether it was a Festival or an ordinary weekday.

chunks.en: So they made a rule that they would accept witnesses
chunks.st: From that point on, the Sages instituted that they would accept testimony to determine the start of the month

chunks.en: only until Minchah time.
chunks.st: only until minḥa
chunks.stMore: time. If witnesses had not arrived by that hour, they would declare Elul a thirty-day month and calculate the dates of the Festivals accordingly.

chunks.he: וְאִם בָּאוּ עֵדִים מִן הַמִּנְחָה וּלְמַעְלָה,
chunks.en: And if witnesses came from Minchah time on,
chunks.st: And if witnesses came from minḥa time onward,
chunks.stMore: although the calculations for the dates of the Festivals would begin from the following day, the people would nevertheless

chunks.he: נוֹהֲגִין אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם קֹדֶשׁ וּלְמָחָר קֹדֶשׁ.
chunks.en: they kept that day holy, and the next day holy too.
chunks.st: observe that day, on which the witnesses arrived, as sacred, so that in future years they would not treat the entire day as a weekday and engage in labor from the morning on the assumption that the witnesses will arrive only after minḥa time. And they would also observe the following day as sacred.
chunks.stMore: On the second day, they observed Rosh HaShana in full, both by sacrificing its offerings as well as by calculating the upcoming Festivals from that date.

chunks.en: After the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
chunks.st: After the Temple was destroyed
chunks.stMore: and there was no longer any reason for this ordinance,

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made a rule
chunks.st: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted

chunks.he: שֶׁיְּהוּ מְקַבְּלִין עֵדוּת הַחֹדֶשׁ כָּל הַיּוֹם.
chunks.en: that they would accept witnesses for the new moon all day long.
chunks.st: that they would once again accept testimony to determine the start of the month the entire day.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa said:

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
chunks.st: And this, too, Rabban

chunks.en: also made this rule:
chunks.st: Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ רֹאשׁ בֵּית דִּין בְּכָל מָקוֹם,
chunks.en: that even if the head of the Beis Din is somewhere else,
chunks.st: that even if the head of the court of seventy-one is in any other place, not where the Great Sanhedrin is in session,

chunks.en: the witnesses should go
chunks.st: the witnesses should nevertheless go

chunks.en: only to the place where the Beis Din gathers.
chunks.st: only to the place where the Great Sanhedrin gathers
chunks.stMore: to deliver testimony to determine the start of the month. Although the date of the month is dependent on the head of the Great Sanhedrin, as it is he who declares that the month is sanctified (see 24a), nevertheless, Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted that the members of the Great Sanhedrin may sanctify the month in the absence of the head of the court.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches the order of the brachos in Musaf of Rosh Hashanah, with Malchiyos, Zichronos and Shofaros, and where the shofar is blown. Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri and Rabbi Akiva disagree about where Malchiyos goes.

chunks.en: The order of the brachos:
chunks.st: The order of the blessings
chunks.stMore: of the additional prayer on Rosh HaShana is as follows:

chunks.en: He says Avos, Gevuros, and Kedushas Hashem,
chunks.st: One recites the blessing of the Patriarchs, the blessing of God’s Mighty Deeds, and the blessing of the Sanctification of God’s Name, all of which are recited all year long.

words.note: The first bracha of Shemoneh Esrei, about our fathers.
The second bracha, about Hashem's mighty deeds.

chunks.en: and he puts Malchiyos together with them,
chunks.st: And one includes the blessing of Kingship, containing many biblical verses on that theme, with them,
chunks.stMore: i.e., in the blessing of the Sanctification of God’s Name,

words.note: Pesukim about Hashem as King.

chunks.en: and he does not blow the shofar.
chunks.st: and he does not sound the shofar after it.

chunks.en: Then Kedushas HaYom,
chunks.st: Next, one adds a special blessing for the Sanctification of the Day,

chunks.en: and he blows. Then Zichronos,
chunks.st: and sounds the shofar after it; followed by the blessing of Remembrances,
chunks.stMore: which contains many biblical verses addressing that theme,

words.note: Pesukim about Hashem remembering.

chunks.en: and he blows. Then Shofaros,
chunks.st: and sounds the shofar after it; and recites the blessing of Shofarot,
chunks.stMore: which includes verses that mention the shofar,

words.note: Pesukim about the shofar.

chunks.he: וְתוֹקֵעַ. וְאוֹמֵר עֲבוֹדָה וְהוֹדָאָה וּבִרְכַּת כֹּהֲנִים,
chunks.en: and he blows. Then he says Avodah, Hodaah, and Birkas Kohanim.
chunks.st: and sounds the shofar after it. And he then returns to the regular Amida prayer and recites the blessing of God’s Service and the blessing of Thanksgiving and the Priestly Blessing.

words.note: The bracha of thanks, Modim.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to him:

chunks.en: "If he does not blow for Malchiyos,
chunks.st: If one does not sound the shofar for the blessing of Kingship,

chunks.en: why does he say it there?
chunks.st: why does he mention it?

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אוֹמֵר אָבוֹת וּגְבוּרוֹת וּקְדֻשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם,
chunks.en: Rather, he says Avos, Gevuros, and Kedushas Hashem,
chunks.st: Rather, the order of the blessings is as follows: One recites the blessing of the Patriarchs and that of God’s Mighty Deeds and that of the Sanctification of God’s Name.

chunks.en: and puts Malchiyos together with Kedushas HaYom,
chunks.st: He subsequently includes the blessing of Kingship in the blessing of the Sanctification of the Day,

chunks.en: and he blows. Then Zichronos,
chunks.st: and sounds the shofar. Next he recites the blessing of Remembrances,

chunks.en: and he blows. Then Shofaros,
chunks.st: and sounds the shofar after it, and the blessing of Shofarot

chunks.he: וְתוֹקֵעַ. וְאוֹמֵר עֲבוֹדָה וְהוֹדָאָה וּבִרְכַּת כֹּהֲנִים:
chunks.en: and he blows. Then he says Avodah, Hodaah, and Birkas Kohanim."
chunks.st: and sounds the shofar after it. He then recites the blessing of God’s Service and the blessing of Thanksgiving and the Priestly Blessing.

mishnayos.summary: In each of Malchiyos, Zichronos and Shofaros we say ten pesukim, starting from the Torah and ending with the Nevi'im. We do not use pesukim about punishment.

chunks.en: We do not say fewer than ten pesukim of Malchiyos,
chunks.st: One does not recite fewer than ten verses in theblessing of Kingship,

chunks.en: or fewer than ten of Zichronos,
chunks.st: or fewer than ten verses in the blessing of Remembrances,

chunks.en: or fewer than ten of Shofaros.
chunks.st: or fewer than ten verses in the blessing of Shofarot.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says:

chunks.en: "If he said three of each one,
chunks.st: If one recited three from each of them,

chunks.en: he has done the mitzvah." We do not say pesukim of Zichronos, Malchiyos,
chunks.st: he has fulfilled his obligation. One does not mention verses of Remembrance, Kingship,

chunks.en: or Shofaros that are about punishment.
chunks.st: and Shofar that have a theme of punishment.

chunks.en: He starts with the Torah and ends with the Navi.
chunks.st: When reciting the ten verses, one begins with verses from the Torah and concludes with verses from the Prophets.

words.note: The books of the Nevi'im, the Prophets.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: "If he ended with the Torah, he has done the mitzvah."
chunks.st: If he concluded with a verse from the Torah, he has fulfilled his obligation.

mishnayos.summary: On Rosh Hashanah, the chazzan of Musaf is the one who has the shofar blown. On days with Hallel, the chazzan of Shacharis says Hallel.

chunks.en: The chazzan who leads the davening on the Yom Tov
chunks.st: With regard to one who is passing before the ark, as prayer leader,

words.note: The place where the chazzan stands.

chunks.en: of Rosh Hashanah:
chunks.st: on the festival of Rosh HaShana,

chunks.en: the second one has the shofar blown.
chunks.explain: The chazzan of Musaf.
chunks.st: it is the second prayer leader, i.e., the one who leads the additional prayer, who sounds the shofar on behalf of the congregation.

chunks.en: And at the time of Hallel,
chunks.st: And on a day when the hallel is recited,

chunks.en: the first one leads Hallel.
chunks.explain: The chazzan of Shacharis.
chunks.st: the first prayer leader, i.e., the one who leads the morning prayer, recites the hallel on behalf of the congregation.

mishnayos.summary: We may not break the rules of Shabbos or Yom Tov to get a shofar ready for Rosh Hashanah. Children may blow the shofar to learn, and one must blow with the mitzvah in mind.

chunks.en: For the shofar of Rosh Hashanah,
chunks.st: With regard to the shofar of Rosh HaShana,

chunks.en: we may not walk past the Shabbos limit for it,
chunks.st: one may not pass the Shabbat limit for it, i.e., to go and hear it,

words.note: The Shabbos limit: how far one may walk out of town.

chunks.en: and we may not clear away a pile of stones for it.
chunks.st: nor may one clear a pile of rubble to uncover a buried shofar.

chunks.en: We may not climb a tree,
chunks.st: One may not climb a tree,

chunks.en: or ride on an animal,
chunks.st: nor may one ride on an animal,

chunks.en: or swim in the water.
chunks.st: nor may one swim in water, in order to find a shofar to sound.

chunks.en: And we may not cut it, whether
chunks.st: And one may not cut the shofar to prepare it for use,

chunks.en: with something the Rabbis forbade,
chunks.st: neither with an object that is prohibited due to a rabbinic decree

words.note: Shevus: something the Rabbis forbade on Shabbos and Yom Tov.

chunks.he: וּבֵין בְּדָבָר שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוּם לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
chunks.en: or with something the Torah forbids.
chunks.st: nor with an object that may not be used due to a prohibition by Torah law.

chunks.en: But if he wants to put
chunks.st: However, if one wishes to place

chunks.en: water or wine into it,
chunks.explain: To make it sound clear.
chunks.st: water or wine into
chunks.stMore: the shofar on Rosh HaShana so that it emits a clear sound,

chunks.he: יִתֵּן. אֵין מְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַתִּינוֹקוֹת מִלִּתְקוֹעַ,
chunks.en: he may put it. We do not stop children from blowing,
chunks.st: he may place it, as this does not constitute a prohibited labor. One need not prevent children from sounding
chunks.stMore: the shofar on Rosh HaShana, despite the fact that they are not obligated in mitzvot.

chunks.en: but we help them until they learn.
chunks.st: Rather, one occupies himself with them, encouraging and instructing them, until they learn how to sound it properly.

chunks.en: Someone who blows without meaning to do the mitzvah has not done it,
chunks.st: The mishna adds: One who acts unawares and sounds the shofar without any intention to perform the mitzva has not fulfilled his obligation.

words.en: and one who is just blowing
words.note: Blowing without meaning to do the mitzvah.

chunks.en: and someone who hears it from him
chunks.st: And, similarly, one who hears the shofar blasts from one who acts unawares

chunks.en: has not done the mitzvah.
chunks.st: has not fulfilled his obligation.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches the order and length of the shofar blasts. It also teaches that every person must daven Musaf, while Rabban Gamliel says the chazzan does it for everyone.

chunks.en: The order of the blasts
chunks.st: The order of the blasts

chunks.en: is three sets of three each.
chunks.explain: Tekiah, teruah, tekiah.
chunks.st: is three sets of three blasts each, which are: Tekia, terua, and tekia.

chunks.en: A tekiah is as long as three teruos.
chunks.st: The length of a tekia is equal to the length of three teruot,

words.note: A long, straight blast.

chunks.en: A teruah is as long as three crying sounds.
chunks.st: and the length of a terua is equal to the length of three whimpers.

words.note: A blast of short sounds.

chunks.en: If he blew the first tekiah,
chunks.st: If one sounded the first
chunks.stMore: tekia of the initial series of tekia, terua, tekia,

chunks.en: and made the second one as long as two,
chunks.st: and then extended the second tekia of that series to the length of two
chunks.stMore: tekiot, so that it should count as both the second tekia of the first set and the first tekia of the second set,

chunks.en: it counts as only one.
chunks.st: he has in his hand the fulfillment of only one
chunks.stMore: tekia, and he must begin the second set with a new tekia.

chunks.en: Someone who said the brachos, and afterward
chunks.st: With regard to one who recited the blessings of the additional prayer, and only afterward

chunks.en: got a shofar,
chunks.st: a shofar became available to him,

chunks.en: blows tekiah, teruah, tekiah three times.
chunks.st: he sounds a tekia, sounds a terua, and sounds a tekia, an order he repeats three times.

chunks.en: Just as the chazzan must daven,
chunks.st: Just as the prayer leader is obligated in the prayer of Rosh HaShana,

words.note: The chazzan.

chunks.en: so every single person must daven.
chunks.st: so too, each and every individual is obligated in these prayers.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel disagrees and says:

chunks.en: The chazzan does the mitzvah
chunks.st: Individuals are not obligated, as the prayer leader fulfills the obligation

chunks.en: for everyone.
chunks.st: on behalf of the many.
